You are a READ-ONLY code reviewer. Do NOT modify any files. Review ONLY the diff below for ONE angle: **Reuse** — new code that re-implements something the codebase already has. Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change; name the existing helper to call instead.

Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim. The change transports two Andes CSRs (mcache_ctl 0x7CA, mmisc_ctl 0x7D0) across the QEMU->vsim hybrid handoff. It deliberately mirrors how `fcsr`/`mscratch`/the L24 trap CSRs are already transported.

Files to consider (read them + adjacent code as needed):
- include/hybrid/state_abi.h, include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h
- qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c (resolve_handles, drain_state_into, read_reg64, find_reg)
- verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp (write_csr_tolerant, write_csr_abstract_or_pb)
- verilator/tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp, verilator/tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp

DIFF UNDER REVIEW:
```
state_abi.h: added `uint64_t mcache_ctl; uint64_t mmisc_ctl;` after fcsr; reserved[208]->[192].
state_abi_check.h: added offset asserts for mcache_ctl(+48)/mmisc_ctl(+56), reserved(+64); updated size comment.
hybrid_handoff.c: added VcpuRegs fields mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl; resolve_handles: v->mcache_ctl=find_reg(regs,"mcache_ctl"); v->mmisc_ctl=find_reg(regs,"mmisc_ctl"); drain_state_into: s.mcache_ctl=read_reg64(v->mcache_ctl); s.mmisc_ctl=read_reg64(v->mmisc_ctl);
resume_driver.hpp: added constants kCsrMcacheCtl=0x7CA, kCsrMmiscCtl=0x7D0; in resume(): write_csr_tolerant(kCsrMcacheCtl,state.mcache_ctl); write_csr_tolerant(kCsrMmiscCtl,state.mmisc_ctl);
resume_driver.test.cpp: new TEST_CASE asserting the two CSR write-COMMANDs (pattern copied from the L24 test: loop over {csr,val} pairs, find write-COMMAND, check DATA0/DATA1).
state_abi.test.cpp: split the "fcsr...before reserved" test; added a new TEST_CASE checking mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl/reserved adjacency.
```

The new TEST_CASE in resume_driver.test.cpp duplicates the find-write-COMMAND-then-check-DATA0/DATA1 loop that the L23 (mscratch) and L24 (mepc/...) tests already use. Assess: is there an existing test helper for "assert CSR X was written with value V via abstract command" that the new test (and ideally the L24 test) should call instead? If so, name it with file:line. If no such helper exists and each test open-codes the loop, say so (then it's an existing pattern, not a new duplication — note that).

Return a short findings list: each with file, line, one-line summary, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated and the existing helper to use). If the code is already DRY and correctly reuses existing patterns, say so explicitly. Be precise; do not invent helpers that don't exist — verify by reading.

1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 2 (L11): vreg[] widened from 64 to 128 bytes per register, which
25	// shifts every field after it. Readers reject version-1 files loudly (all
26	// three consumers check magic + version + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
27	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 2u
28	
29	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64 (1u << 0)
30	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP   (1u << 1)
31	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V    (1u << 2)
32	
33	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
34	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
35	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
36	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
37	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
38	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
39	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
40	
41	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
42	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
43	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
44	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
45	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
46	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
47	
48	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
49	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
50	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
51	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
52	
53	// All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
54	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
55	// the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
56	struct hybrid_state_v1 {
57	  uint32_t magic;
58	  uint32_t version;
59	  uint32_t flags;
60	  uint32_t hart_id;
61	  uint64_t pc;
62	  uint64_t priv;  // 0=U, 1=S, 3=M
63	
64	  uint64_t gpr[32];
65	  uint64_t fpr[32];
66	
67	  uint64_t mstatus;
68	  uint64_t mepc;
69	  uint64_t mtvec;
70	  uint64_t mcause;
71	  uint64_t mtval;
72	  uint64_t mscratch;
73	  uint64_t medeleg;
74	  uint64_t mideleg;
75	  uint64_t mip;
76	  uint64_t mie;
77	  uint64_t mcycle;
78	  uint64_t minstret;
79	  uint64_t satp;
80	
81	  uint64_t pmpcfg[HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM];
82	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];
83	
84	  uint64_t vstart;
85	  uint64_t vtype;
86	  uint64_t vl;
87	  uint64_t vlenb;
88	  uint8_t  vreg[32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX];
89	  uint64_t vxsat;
90	  uint64_t vxrm;
91	  uint64_t vcsr;
92	
93	  // F13: warmup-window snapshot of cycle/instret counters, captured K insns
94	  // after vsim entry. Drain-only metadata; ResumeDriver never restores them.
95	  // Both zero when --vsim-warmup-icount=0 or the workload exited inside the
96	  // warmup window. Consumes 16 bytes from the original 232-byte reserved tail.
97	  uint64_t mcycle_at_measure_start;
98	  uint64_t minstret_at_measure_start;
99	
100	  // L20: FP control/status -- frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], live when
101	  // HYBRID_FLAG_FP is set. Drained by the plugin, restored by ResumeDriver,
102	  // re-read by StateDrain. Pre-L20 state files carry 0 here (reserved bytes
103	  // are written as zero), which reads back as the reset value (RNE, no
104	  // flags) -- exactly the old behavior, so no version bump.
105	  uint64_t fcsr;
106	
107	  // Andes machine setup CSRs that crt0 writes once at boot and the program
108	  // then runs under: mcache_ctl (0x7CA) enables the L1 I/D caches, mmisc_ctl
109	  // (0x7D0) holds misc machine config. Drained by the plugin, restored by
110	  // ResumeDriver. Without these the cycle engine resumes at the ROI with
111	  // caches DISABLED (its reset default) because the enabling write happened
112	  // on the functional engine, which has no cache model -- inflating the
113	  // measured window severalfold. Old state files carry 0 here (reserved
114	  // bytes read back as zero), i.e. "leave at the hart's reset value", which
115	  // is the pre-existing behavior, so no version bump. Restored tolerantly:
116	  // an engine without these custom CSRs mirrors the write as a no-op.
117	  uint64_t mcache_ctl;
118	  uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
119	
120	  uint8_t  reserved[192];  // zero-initialise on write; 256 - 3*8 (vxsat/vxrm/vcsr) - 2*8 (warmup) - 8 (fcsr) - 2*8 (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl)
121	};
122	
123	#ifdef __cplusplus
124	}  // extern "C"
125	#endif
126	
127	#include "hybrid/state_abi_check.h"
128	
129	#endif  // HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
130

2	// hybrid handoff tests (insn_match, csr_trigger, handoff_controller) to
3	// construct the marker HINTs -- and near-miss variants -- with explicit

9	#include <cstdint>
10	#include <span>

12	namespace hybrid::test
13	{

15	// slti rd, rs1, imm: OP-IMM (0x13), funct3=010, imm[31:20]. The marker
16	// HINTs pin rd=rs1=x0; the explicit fields let tests build near-misses.
17	inline constexpr auto encode_slti(uint32_t rd, uint32_t rs1, uint32_t imm)
18	  -> uint32_t
19	{
20	  return (imm << 20) | (rs1 << 15) | (0b010u << 12) | (rd << 7) | 0x13u;
21	}
22	
23	template<std::size_t N>
24	auto as_bytes(const std::array<uint32_t, N>& a) -> std::span<const uint8_t>
25	{
26	  return std::span{reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t*>(a.data()),
27	                   N * sizeof(uint32_t)};
28	}

## Reuse review: mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl transport

Verdict: the production code is DRY -- it correctly reuses every existing helper and convention. The one duplication is in the test, and it is a pre-existing open-coded pattern, not a new one introduced by this diff.

### Production side -- correct reuse (no findings)

- `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:240-241` -- calls the existing `write_csr_tolerant` (defined `:293-297`), the same helper mtvec/mscratch/mepc/mcause/mtval/mie/mip use. Does NOT re-implement the abstract-write-then-clear-cmderr dance. The `kCsrMcacheCtl`/`kCsrMmiscCtl` constants (`:60-61`) follow the existing `kCsr*` block convention. Correct, and `write_csr_tolerant` (not `write_csr_abstract_or_pb`) is the right pick given the "engine without these custom CSRs mirrors as no-op" requirement.
- `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:236-237` and `:392-393` -- reuse the existing `find_reg` and `read_reg64` exactly like every other CSR. No duplication.
- `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h:69-77` -- offset asserts follow the existing per-field convention verbatim. Correct.

### Test side -- one finding (pre-existing pattern, not a new duplication)

Finding: `verilator/tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp:607-626` (new "Andes cache fix" TEST_CASE)
- Summary: the find-write-COMMAND-then-check-DATA0/DATA1 loop is copied character-for-character from the L24 test at `:567-586` (only the `want[]` array contents differ).
- Existing helper to call instead: none exists. I verified the three candidate headers -- `test_helpers.hpp` (TLM memory access only), `recording_bus.hpp` (a bus double + `kDmstatusHaltedAndAcked` + `SteppingBus`, no assertion helpers), `insn_encoders.hpp` (slti encoder only). The file's own anonymous-namespace helpers (`find_write`, `count_writes_to`, `cmd_regnos`, `contains_regno` at `:152-168, 329-342`) only assert a regno's *presence*; none checks its DATA0/DATA1 *value*.
- Cost: the same value-bearing assertion loop is open-coded in ~6 places already -- DPC `:239-259`, fcsr `:484-492`, mscratch/L23 `:523-542`, mepc/L24 `:567-586`, this new one `:607-626`, dcsr/L6 `:1053-1067`. The new test adds a 6th copy.

Per your own criterion: because no helper exists and every value-checking test open-codes this loop, the new TEST_CASE is following an established pattern, not introducing a new duplication. It is consistent with the surrounding code and not a blocker for this diff.

Optional (pre-existing, out of scope for this change): extracting one helper into the anonymous namespace, e.g.

```
void check_csr_abstract_write(const std::vector<DmiOp>& ops, uint16_t csr, uint64_t val);
```

would collapse all ~6 copies (including L24) and matches the file's existing small-helper style. This is a cleanup of code that predates the diff, so if applied it should be a separate structural commit, not folded into this behavioral change.

One context note (not a finding against this diff): `resume_driver.test.cpp:51-138` defines its own richer `RecordingBus` rather than the shared `tests/hybrid/recording_bus.hpp` one, because it needs the fail-injection features (`fail_csr_write`, `warl_ignore`, `fail_next_pb_exec`) the shared double lacks. The new test reuses that local bus correctly; this divergence is pre-existing.
